notes: kb/Work PB5793 landed. §1985:IV.4.2.1 SR2: the comma and semicolon followed by a space 'are separators that may be used anywhere the separator space is used'; SR9 lets a space follow '(' and SR8 lets one precede ')'. Inside a list region (a subscript list, a reference modifier, an argument list) the lexer kept the separator as the FNARG_SEPARATOR token wherever it stood, and the grammar admits it only between two items, so W-E (I +, 1), W-E (, I) and W-E (I, ) were COBOL0001 at every edition. The lexer now keeps it only at a boundary between two items (CobolLexer.ListItemBoundary: the token before it ends an item and the character after it begins one) and skips it as the space elsewhere. Probed at --std 85: pb5793_list_separator_where_space prints every line as derived.

next.reason: §2023:8.3.5 SR2 repeats 'comma and semicolon, immediately followed by a space, are separators that may be used anywhere the separator space is used', without 1985's 'Except when the comma is used in a PICTURE character-string'. The exception was idle: §1985:IV.4.2.1 (SR9) says 'PICTURE character-strings are delimited only by the separators space, comma, semicolon, or period', and §1985:VI.5.9.5 (insertion editing) requires a final picture comma to be 'immediately followed by the separator period', so comma followed by space is always the separator (2023 keeps the latter as §2023:13.18.40.3 SR7). Same programs accepted and refused.
